title: Locally constructible common-stage adic heart on the separated finite-type open basis
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ and $(\ell,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a scheme over $k_0$. Let $\mathcal B_T$ be its separated finite-type open subschemes (finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] refer to their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$). For $U\in\mathcal B_T$, write $\mathcal H_U=\operatorname{Sh}_c(U,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ for the actual common-stage constructible heart of [def-weil-constructible-heart]. For $U\subseteq V$, let $r_{UV}=L(U\hookrightarrow V)^*$ be the canonical completed common-stage derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the integral-normalized composition comparison of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Define the locally constructible adic heart on $T$ as the category of cartesian local data: an object is a family $K_U\in\mathcal H_U$ with isomorphisms $\rho_{UV}:r_{UV}K_V\simeq K_U$, such that for every $U\subseteq V\subseteq W$ the composite of the canonical comparison $r_{UW}K_W\simeq r_{UV}r_{VW}K_W$, $r_{UV}(\rho_{VW})$ and $\rho_{UV}$ equals $\rho_{UW}$. Repeated opens are included in this requirement, hence give the identity normalization. A morphism is a family $f_U:K_U\to K^{\prime}_U$ satisfying $\rho^{\prime}_{UV}\circ r_{UV}(f_V)=f_U\circ\rho_{UV}$. Identities and composition are componentwise, as are zero arrows; these operations preserve the compatibility equations and the zero arrows are absorbing. Evaluation at $U$ is the functor $K\mapsto K_U$, $f\mapsto f_U$, preserving zero arrows. On a locally finite-type scheme these opens form a basis, and this is the compatible-local-heart description of locally constructible adic sheaves. No single finite coefficient field on all of $T$ is required. The prime $\ell$ is a unit in $k_0$ and its image in each residue field supplies the inverses used by completed restriction. The same unit, transported through the fixed inclusion $k_0\to k$, supplies the residue-field inverses on schemes over $k$, in particular for geometric coefficient fibres.

proof.text: The finite base field has characteristic p: its cardinality is p^a, so apply Mathlib charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow. By CharP.isUnit_natCast_iff the coefficient prime l is a unit, since distinct primes p and l do not divide one another. This proves dlAdicBasePrimeUnit directly from the finite-field datum.

For dlAdicLocalCompatible_multiplicative, identities satisfy compatibility by map_id. For composition, reassociate the square, substitute the two compatibility equations, then use map_comp. These are the category and functor laws on the explicit families.

For dlAdicLocalCompatible_zero, first show that ofHom of a zero representative is zero: apply the injective Hom-coordinate equivalence, use its representative equation, and use that the direct-limit injection is additive. Choose a common coefficient stage for the two objects. The rational pullback is additive by its existing uniqueness specification, so maps the zero representative to zero. The common-stage pullback representative formula conjugates this zero by the comparison isomorphisms, hence also gives zero. Transport across the specified object equalities using HEq. Both sides of the compatibility square are consequently zero.

For dlAdicLocalZeroLaws, use extensionality through the wide subcategory, induced category, and component family. At every open the equations are comp_zero and zero_comp in the ambient common-stage category. Evaluation of the literal zero family is definitionally zero, proving dlAdicLocalEvaluation_zero by reflexivity.
